draft.title: Banking, bills and borrowing
card: Bank accounts
A transaction account holds money for daily spending. A savings account holds money you do not plan to spend soon, and it usually pays interest.
Card payments
A debit card takes money straight from your account. A credit card lends you money, and you must pay it back to the card company.
Bills
A bill is money you owe for a service, such as power or phone. Paying after the due date can add a late fee, so check the date.
Borrowing
If you borrow, you repay more than you borrowed. Example: borrow $500 and repay $550 in total. Borrowing cost $550 − $500 = $50.
draft.remember: Borrowing means repaying more than you borrowed. The extra is the cost of borrowing.

a.q: Tom pays for a $40 meal with his debit card. What happens?
opts: $40 is taken from his account straight away
He borrows $40 and repays the bank later
$40 is added to his savings account interest
He is given 30 days before paying $40
a.why: A debit card takes money directly from the account. The credit card is the one that lends money, so the idea of borrowing and repaying later is wrong for a debit card.
a.clue: Debit and credit cards work differently.

b.q: Priya borrows $2000 for a laptop. She repays $2300 in total. What did the borrowing cost her?
b.why: The cost is the total repaid minus the amount borrowed: $2300 − $2000 = $300. Choosing $2300 gives the total repaid, not the extra cost.
b.clue: Subtract what she borrowed from what she repaid.

a.best: $40 is taken from his account straight away

problems.detail: The Borrowing line says that if you borrow, you repay more than you borrowed. That is not always true: interest-free loans exist, and a credit card paid in full within the interest-free period costs nothing extra. It should say you usually or can repay more.

'Borrowing means repaying more than you borrowed' states as a rule something that is only usually true. Interest-free borrowing has no extra cost, so this line should be softened, for example to 'usually means'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer. The card and the remember line say borrowing always means repaying more, which ignores interest-free loans and credit cards paid off in time, so this should be softened to 'usually'.
